extracted.intended_audience: literary critics, serious readers, and students evaluating novels or studying literary craft
extracted.subtask_description: A checklist-style set of literary particulars for judging novels (style, characterization, sincerity, reader-engagement) illustrated by Mark Twain's questions about Sir Walter Scott; also brief guidance on magazine writing and autobiography craft. Useful for critics and readers assessing fiction and for writers thinking about truthfulness and production conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Passages written in good English (not slovenly or involved)
rubrics_metrics.description: Are there in Sir Walter's novels passages done in good English—English which is neither slovenly or involved?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate sentences for clarity, grammatical soundness, and avoidance of slovenliness or excessive involved construction; the presence of such passages counts positively toward the author's craft.

rubrics_metrics.name: Passages above common quality (not poor, thin, or commonplace)
rubrics_metrics.description: Are there passages whose English is not poor and thin and commonplace, but is of a quality above that?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for prose that rises above cliché and thinness—distinctive phrasing, richness of language, and moments where diction and thought exceed ordinary commonplace writing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Passages that 'burn with real fire' (genuine intensity)
rubrics_metrics.description: Are there passages which burn with real fire—not punk, fox-fire, make believe?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish authentic passion or intensity from artificial or superficial effects; true 'fire' should feel vital and convincing rather than contrived showiness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Heroes and heroines who are not mere cads/cadesses
rubrics_metrics.description: Has he heroes and heroines who are not cads and cadesses?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess main characters for moral and psychological substance; they should transcend shallow, merely immoral or priggish caricature and possess convincing human complexity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistency of character: acts and speech matching description
rubrics_metrics.description: Has he personages whose acts and talk correspond with their characters as described by him?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check that characters' behavior and dialogue align with their established personalities and histories; avoid figures whose actions feel inconsistent or written merely to serve plot convenience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Admirable protagonists with understandable reasons for admiration
rubrics_metrics.description: Has he heroes and heroines whom the reader admires, admires, and knows why?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Good protagonists should inspire admiration for identifiable qualities—courage, wit, integrity—where the reader understands why admiration is merited rather than being asked to admire without cause.

rubrics_metrics.name: Humor: funny characters and genuinely humorous passages
rubrics_metrics.description: Has he funny characters that are funny, and humorous passages that are humorous?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate the authenticity and effectiveness of comic elements: humor should arise naturally from character and situation rather than forced jokes or mere labels of 'funny.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Ability to chain reader's interest (sustained engagement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Does he ever chain the reader's interest, and make him reluctant to lay the book down?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure narrative propulsion and suspense; a successful work will sustain curiosity and investment so readers are reluctant to stop reading.

rubrics_metrics.name: Moments of sincerity: cessation of posing and artificiality
rubrics_metrics.description: Are there pages where he ceases from posing, ceases from admiring the placid flood and flow of his own dilutions, ceases from being artificial, and is for a time, long or short, recognizably sincere and in earnest?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify passages where the author drops mannerisms and self-conscious artifice to speak with genuine feeling or conviction; such moments indicate depth and authenticity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorial knowledge of English versus deliberate neglect
rubrics_metrics.description: Did he know how to write English, and didn't do it because he didn't want to?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider whether lapses in style reflect ignorance or intentional choice; deliberate stylistic choices are defensible, but avoid ascribing poor writing to affectation without evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Word-choice competence: right word selection vs ignorance
rubrics_metrics.description: Did he use the right word only when he couldn't think of another one, or did he run so much to wrong because he didn't know the right one when he saw it?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess precision of diction: frequent wrong or awkward word choices suggest lack of command; judicious, apt word selection shows mastery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Readability with maintained respect (timelessness of reputation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Can you read him? and keep your respect for him? Of course a person could in his day—an era of sentimentality and sloppy romantics—but land! can a body do it today?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge whether a work endures beyond its original audience; consider if modern readers can engage with the text without losing esteem for its artistry or morals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Autobiography: truthfulness 'between the lines'
rubrics_metrics.description: An autobiography is the truest of all books; while it inevitably consists mainly of extinctions of the truth, shirkings of the truth, partial revealments of the truth... the remorseless truth is there, between the lines, where the author is raking dust upon it, the result being that the reader knows the author in spite of his wily diligences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For autobiographical writing, aim for an underlying honesty that shows through even when full disclosure is impossible; authenticity often resides in what is implied and in consistent self-revelation rather than blunt confession.

rubrics_metrics.name: Magazine writing: start right and expect heavy discard
rubrics_metrics.description: Magazining is difficult work because every third page represents 2 pages that you have put in the fire; (because you are nearly sure to start wrong twice) and so when you have finished an article and are willing to let it go to print it represents only 10 cents a word instead of 30.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When writing for magazines, plan for multiple false starts and substantial revision; 'starting right'—beginning with a well-chosen opening and structure—reduces wasted effort and improves the yield of publishable material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Productive conditions: solitude and inspiring environment
rubrics_metrics.description: This secluded and silent solitude this clean, soft air and this enchanting view of Florence, the great valley and the snow-mountains... are the right conditions for work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider physical and environmental conditions (quiet, fresh air, inspiring views) as contributing factors to creative productivity; they can facilitate sustained focus and inspiration.
